TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that guarantees reliable, ordered delivery of data through acknowledgments and retransmissions, while UDP is a connectionless protocol that sends datagrams without guarantees of arrival, order, or duplicate protection. TCP suits applications needing correctness (web, email), whereas UDP favors speed and simplicity for real-time or loss-tolerant traffic (streaming, DNS, gaming).
